name: bespunky-communication
description: How Claude SPEAKS — the output style that pitches every answer to the person actually reading it. Ships `Pitch to the listener`, an output style built on four questions Claude asks itself before composing any response (what type of conversation is this · what is actually being asked · at what depth am I being spoken to · what does this person really need to know), so it enters and exits conversation modes the way a person adjusts their pitch for a listener — and follows the zoom within the turn when an overview is met with a depth question, or fine detail is met with a request for the overview. Two absolute rules hold at every pitch: never use jargon or an abbreviation assuming it is understood unless the user reached for it first, and never assume the user watched you work — an internal process handed over as a bare digested conclusion gives the reader a verdict they cannot connect to anything, so bridge it with the short path from what you looked at to what it means. Register is read off THE MESSAGE, never off a role or a profile: roles are an illustration of pitch, not an input to it. Presentation only — it sets how things are said, never how much design, verification or process the work gets, and `keep-coding-instructions` keeps Claude Code's built-in engineering behaviour intact so it cannot pull against a project's own always-on rules. Installing makes the style AVAILABLE; it is inert until selected with `/output-style` or `outputStyle` in settings — because an output style is exclusive (one active at a time) and taking that slot is the consumer's decision, not the toolkit's.
